title: Space Adaptation Syndrome (SAS) & Vestibular Protocol
trigger_patterns: Crew reports nausea, cold sweating, stomach awareness, or spatial disorientation upon head motion
Graybiel motion sickness score exceeds individual baseline (> 2/10)
Acute mission phase (Mission Days 1-4) neuro-vestibular adaptation monitoring

steps.text: Instruct affected crew member to immediately minimize rapid head and torso rotations, especially pitch and roll axes outside the visual field of reference.
steps.source: LIGHTMINUTE demonstration protocol - not an operational NASA medical procedure

steps.text: Score current neuro-vestibular severity on the Graybiel motion sickness rating scale (0-10) and record in the personal log.
steps.source: LIGHTMINUTE demonstration protocol - not an operational NASA medical procedure

steps.text: Anchor feet in crew quarters or sleep station restraint to provide solid somatosensory proprioceptive reference points.
steps.source: LIGHTMINUTE demonstration protocol - not an operational NASA medical procedure

steps.text: Review onboard antiemetic options: consider promethazine or ondansetron per medical kit guidelines. Note: promethazine has strong sedative effects; restrict from piloting or airlock operations for 12 hours.
steps.source: LIGHTMINUTE demonstration protocol - not an operational NASA medical procedure

steps.text: Initiate paced oral hydration with electrolyte solution (small frequent sips, 100 mL every 20 minutes) to counteract vomiting dehydration.
steps.source: LIGHTMINUTE demonstration protocol - not an operational NASA medical procedure

steps.text: Temporarily reallocate high-cognitive or safety-critical mission tasks to crewmates until vestibular adaptation stabilizes (typically 48 to 72 hours post-orbital insertion).
steps.source: LIGHTMINUTE demonstration protocol - not an operational NASA medical procedure
